control_d4: d=4, frak q=1 (qbar=1): Omega = 1.482859930917321822978577 - 0.5725600144929307091324098 i => frak w = Omega/2 = 0.741429965458660911489288 - 0.286280007246465354566205 i (both master equations, 39 digits agree). Matches KS 0.741420 - 0.286280i in Im to 6 digits but Re differs by 1.0e-5 (0.741430 vs 0.741420): we believe KS line 2100 has a one-digit typo. Supporting: (i) our Z_S at d=4 is symbolically identical to KS eq. (Zequation), and an independent Kodama-Ishibashi master equation gives the same root to 39 digits; (ii) Morgan et al. 0907.5011 Table tab3a lists d_M=5, frak q(Morgan)=2 (= our qbar=1) as 1.48286 - 0.57256i, i.e. frak w = 0.74143, agreeing with us, not 0.741420.
branch_check: Each d tracked in qbar from qbar=0.02 (start guess = first-order hydro Omega = q/sqrt(d-1) - i (d-2)/(d(d-1)) q^2) by natural-parameter continuation (adaptive step <=0.25, linear predictor, step halved if corrector moved >25% of the last increment); d=6 re-tracked with max step 0.01: same values. Small-qbar check: Re Omega/(v_s q) - 1 and -Im Omega/(Gamma q^2) - 1 scale exactly as qbar^2 (ratio 4.00 between qbar=0.02 and 0.01) for d=3,3.5,4,4.5,5 and between 0.01 and 0.005 for d=6, with v_s^2=1/(d-1), Gamma=(d-2)/(d(d-1)). WARNING (surprise): at d=6 the continuously followed sound pole becomes strongly damped: qbar=3 -> 11.8488 - 8.2187i. The weakly damped pole at d=6, qbar=3 is 8.135385546144508119200060026 - 1.221057085620792328184502183i; followed back in qbar at d=6 it goes to the first NON-hydro pole (5.1017 - 2.5888i at qbar=0.5), but followed in d at fixed qbar=3 from d=5 it is the continuation of the d=5 sound pole. qbar-tracking gives the weakly damped branch at qbar=3 for d=5.25 and 5.5 and the strongly damped one for d=5.75 and 6, so the sound pole and the first non-hydro pole exchange identity (pole collision / exceptional point) at some real (d*, qbar*) with 5.5<d*<5.75, roughly 1.5<qbar*<3. Reported d=6 values follow the brief: continuous in qbar from small qbar.
